text:
Evan (ACME): Hey team, we started seeing failed vector inserts after moving a subset of traffic to Dedicated yesterday. Hosted embeddings are 1536 dims, Dedicated calls are returning 1024 dims, downstream DB throws an error. Can you advise?

Maya S: sorry you're hitting this Evan — can you paste the exact API call + response body (redact keys)? quick check: are you specifying model param or relying on default?

Evan (ACME): here's a curl we used (redacted key):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"input": "Our sample text", "deployment": "dedicated-eu-west-1"}'
```
Response snippet: `{"embedding": [0.12, ...], "length": 1024}` — our hosted logs show length 1536 for same text.

Jess H: thanks. Two quick asks: 1) which SDK/version? 2) can you share a base64 or first 8 dims so we can fingerprint model family?

Evan (ACME): JS SDK 2.1.0. First dims (hosted): [0.001, -0.23, 0.11, 0.02, -0.004, 0.9, 0.001, -0.12]
Dedicated first dims: [0.002, -0.19, 0.07, 0.015, -0.002, 0.88, 0.0009, -0.11]

Carlos R: tagging eng-ml @Priya — this looks like a model variant mismatch rather than numeric drift. Could be routing sent to an older quantized variant on Dedicated.

Priya N: I pulled routing logs for dedicated-eu-west-1 around 2026-01-31 08:00-12:00 UTC. There are fallbacks to `embed-compact-1024-q4` when capacity dipped. Hosted defaults to `embed-pro-1536-fp16`. The fallback path didn't include a dimension compatibility check, so requests succeeded but produced 1024-dim vectors.

Maya S: Oof. That explains parity. Evan, sorry for the disruption. For immediate mitigation, can you explicitly set the `model` param to `embed-pro-1536-fp16` in your request? That will pin to the hosted-quality variant where available. Example:
```json
{"input": "...", "model": "embed-pro-1536-fp16"}
```
If Dedicated doesn't have capacity for that model, you'll see an error instead of silent mismatch.

Evan (ACME): thanks — pinning works for our quickpatch. But we need the platform to avoid silent dim changes. Many of our pipelines assume fixed dimension.

Jess H: agreed. I've opened an internal ticket to add a dimension validation in the router. Short-term fix: return 409 / error if chosen model variant has a different embedding size than the advertised API model. Longer-term: make routing prefer parity-first policies.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: PR #4521 — add-dim-check-to-router — to staging at 2026-01-31T16:40:00Z

Carlos R: also found a billing oddity — billing-bot, can you confirm if we billed per-vector based on advertised dimension or actual payload? Evan reported unexpectedly higher embedding storage usage after reconciling.

billing-bot: billing noticed inconsistencies. For requests that were routed to 1024 variants but stored as 1536 in customer's datastore (due to client-side normalization), our ingestion counted the stored size. We're launching an audit for customers with mixed deployments.

Priya N: root cause summary: smart routing allowed capacity-based fallback to a smaller-dimension quantized model without validating output shape. That was intentional to keep calls non-failing, but breaks embedding schema assumptions.

Carlos R: repro steps for eng teams — follow these to reproduce locally:
1) Create Dedicated pool with capacity limit and set routing policy to allow fallback.
2) Configure customer default model to `embed-pro-1536-fp16`.
3) Reduce pool capacity (simulate busy).
4) Send identical embedding requests to hosted vs dedicated endpoints.
Expected: hosted -> 1536, dedicated (fallback) -> 1024.
Logs:
```
2026-01-31T09:04:02Z router INFO selected_variant embed-compact-1024-q4 (fallback due to pool_busy) request_id=...
2026-01-31T09:04:02Z serving INFO returned_embedding_length 1024 request_id=...
```

Priya N: fix landed in staging PR #4521 adds check in router and a hard fail when variant.dim != requested_model.dim plus metrics (counts of failed-vs-allowed-fallbacks). Also added an operator flag to opt-in to lenient behavior temporarily.

Jess H: customer-facing remediation steps for Evan: 1) pin model param in requests to avoid implicit fallback, 2) if you rely on Dedicated, set an assertion in your pipeline to validate vector length and alert before ingestion, 3) we can backfill missing vectors if you want (support will coordinate).

Evan (ACME): appreciate the clear steps. Do you have ETA for the router change to hit prod? This impacts nightly batch jobs.

Carlos R: aiming for staging smoke now, prod rollout 2026-02-02 02:00 UTC (low traffic window). We'll keep you posted.

Maya S: opened support ticket #SUP-12944 for backfill + temporary credits if billing audit finds overcharge. Evan, I'll DM you for details about a backfill window.

Evan (ACME): DM received, thanks. Quick q: any guidance on batching to avoid triggering fallback? Our job sends 10k small docs in bursts.

Priya N: batching guidance — don't batch so large that it exceeds dedicated pool per-request token limit. For Dedicated, tune `batch_size` smaller (e.g., 64-128) and use streaming where possible. Also enable prefix/KV caching to reduce per-request compute. Example Python snippet we recommended:
```python
resp = client.embeddings.create(input=batch, model=\"embed-pro-1536-fp16\", batch_size=128, timeout=45)
```
If requests time out/retry spike, router will see pool pressure and current behavior triggered fallback. Reducing batch size flattens concurrency.

Jess H: follow-ups: I'll send a short KB article with: pinning model param, assertion snippet, batch-size suggestions, and contact for backfills.

billing-bot: audit kickoff queued — relevant accounts: ACME Corp (evan@acme). We'll reach out with any credit recommendations.

Evan (ACME): thanks all — appreciate the fast turnaround. Please keep me posted on prod rollout.

Maya S: will do. closing loop when prod deploy completes and billing audit finishes. :white_check_mark:
